changelog.change: Rebased memory overlay onto corrected native-foundations 0e2ab32b9d57dee3: authored machine-integration-native-foundations.patch (content-identical rebased machine increment; original machine-integration.patch retained frozen), integrated runtime profiles positive/negative prepared via standard tool (bf86b42f/d3dbe302), runner binding moved from retired memory-only prefix manifest to the standard integrated record.

cache_sync collision rename (Main-approved, mechanical); final composition fixed to memory+LCD/CAM service overlay so consumer evidence binds one binary; prepared e1113009 positive and 4dd2fdcb negative-spi1 checkouts via standard tool (47/46 patches, 42 copies, 107 applied targets).

Added UART-owned GDMA TX-info extension triple per Main direction (lcd-cam EspGdmaTxInfo dependency); re-prepared positive e254504f and negative 05e66908 (92/91 inputs, 107 applied targets); superseded e111/4dd2 checkouts preserved with logs.

Main decision C/B split: CORE-04 qualifies on memory-only ca1b66b2 positive / 6f5b2898 negative (frozen gdma engine and 16-case test untouched); camera-capable tree waits for RubberSwallow i2c restack; lcd-cam overlay NOT scope-cut.

CPU PSRAM data-path fix: cache MMU translate/invalidate now target address_space_memory with the committed PSRAM bytes aliased at the private ESP32S3_PSRAM_PHYS_BASE (above the 32-bit guest space) instead of an address space rooted in the uninitialised psram_cpu region. Ordinary IDF6.1 quad8MiB firmware previously took LoadStorePIFAddrError on the first PSRAM access; the fixture leaf now reaches the real cache path with zero panics and live cache-line traffic.

Fixture probe correction (memory_native.c): the unmapped-alias probe is now selected from the actual MMU table and never uses the last DROM entry, which IDF image_process owns as a transient boot-partition map page (MMU_LL_END_DROM_ENTRY_ID); the gdma_unmapped negative rows therefore test a proved-unmapped page.

Re-prepared candidates on the fixed memory inputs: CORE-04 positive ede49916d8240f89 (45 patches/35 copies) and negative-spi1 72c96aa9fc2f9a5e; camera-phase lcdcam positive 6054e4d32ef03a66 (51 patches/50 copies). ca1b66b2/6f5b2898 and the superseded e254/4dd2/e111/bf86 checkouts preserved with their logs.

Native memory qtest address-programming fix: SPI_MEM_ADDR.USR_ADDR_VALUE is the full 32-bit field (pinned register definition FIELD(...,0,32)), so pio()/duplex_read() write the address directly instead of the stale addr<<8 shift. The controller/model side was already register-correct; the shift put SSI writes at 256x the intended physical offset, invisible to PIO-vs-PIO comparisons but fatal to the SSI/GDMA shared-backing asserts. 12/12 memory cases pass on fcdc47b8.

PSRAM system-physical alias base corrected to 0x30000000: the CPU physical address space is 32-bit (TARGET_PHYS_ADDR_SPACE_BITS), so the earlier above-4GiB base was unreachable and ordinary IDF PSRAM startup failed its own memory test. 0x30000000 is private to the model (no guest cache window maps it) and validated end-to-end by the fixture leaf. Re-prepared CORE-04 6dfa7350 positive / 7182364c negative-spi1.

Host runner contract hardening (run-native-fixture.py): live session artifacts (guest log, QEMU stdout/stderr) are written to native disk and published into the evidence directory after the session closes, transient drvfs read faults are retried, and the unmapped-alias row now requires an MMU-table-verified page (entry_invalid=1, ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND, DROM window, not IDF's transient boot-partition entry).

Review fixes on the CORE-04 inputs: the IOMMU UNMAP event's translated_addr now uses the same ESP32S3_PSRAM_PHYS_BASE rebase as the live translation (notifier consumers saw the chip-linear offset), and the header documents the private alias's guest reachability (no private window exists on a 32-bit physical space). Re-prepared CORE-04 positive aa8b5f8e5c99d410 / negative-spi1 1a8fa5bd6f43c42b; 12/12 memory + 16/16 GDMA qtests and 3/3 boot controls pass on it; 4/4 SDK leaves re-run.
